name: Do Won Kim
roles: PhD Candidate in Information, University of Maryland
Student Affiliate, Institute for Trustworthy AI in Law & Society (TRAILS)
Advised by Giovanni Luca Ciampaglia and Cody Buntain
bio: I am a computational social scientist studying how AI and digital information environments shape people’s beliefs and behavior—and how we can redesign these environments to support informed decision-making and strengthen democracy.
In my dissertation, I use experiments and computational methods to design and test interventions that reduce engagement with unreliable sources, bridge partisan divides, and build trust in elections.

I also study ranking and recommendation algorithms, in projects such as the Prosocial Ranking Challenge and research on using large language models to align news-feed recommendations with users’ stated values. I am also interested in how AI is reshaping the production and dissemination of scientific knowledge.
